newsitem.title: UK: Cammell Laird rises to premium on LSE debut.
newsitem.headline: Cammell Laird rises to premium on LSE debut.

text.p: Shares in ship repair group Cammell Laird Plc on Monday climbed to a 14.5 percent premium on their first day of dealings on the London Stock Exchange, dealers said.
Cammell shares, issued at 100p, rose 14-1/2p to 114-1/2p by 1115 GMT in volume of 1.7 million shares.
Dealers said support for the shares in the Birkenhead-based group had come from both institutions and private investors from the north-west of England.
Cammell, valued at around 21.2 million stg at the issue price, had seen its profits grow from 175,000 stg in the year ended April 30 1995 to two million for the 1997 fiscal year.

The group currently has one dry dock in operation which is running at 95 percent capacity but the ship repairer said the restoration of two dry docks would significantly boost its profit growth when they come on stream later in the year.

Cammell said it had won its first ever military contract in 1997 and gained a conversion contract from Falcon Drilling Company Inc, a leading operator of oil exploration and extraction vessels based in Houston. The Group said the Falcon contract was one of the largest it had ever undertaken.
